# quant-fidelity-suite — a receipt-backed yardstick for quantization quality

> Tools, published measurements, and a schema-enforced registry for measuring how far a
> quantized model's output distribution has moved from its unquantized reference, using
> KL divergence over the full vocabulary. Three model families (GLM-5.3-Flash,
> Qwen3.8-27B, and a 5B MoE CI fixture), six storage formats, 75 published rows. Every
> number links to a JSON receipt with pinned revisions and sha256 digests. MIT licensed.
> The registry is a public HF dataset.
>
> **If you are about to measure something, read "Before you rent" in the README first.**
> A measurement needs a panel you can download, a reader for the artifact's storage
> surface *on the lane you can run*, and a profile for that surface at that bit rate.
> Only one panel is fetchable today (`panel--glm53.brandonmusic.final25`); the
> Qwen3.8-27B panels are private; the local lanes read only unquantized or
> payload-store trees, so `bin/measure` cannot execute a third-party quant measurement
> and hands off to `bin/measure-cloud`.

If you are an agent asked to compare quantizations, rank them, or produce a fidelity number,
read the five rules below before you use any number from this project. They are not style
preferences: each one exists because violating it produced a wrong answer that we published
or nearly published, and each is enforced mechanically by the tooling.

**Rule 1 — a KLD number is meaningless without its tuple.** Two numbers are comparable only
if they share panel, reference/teacher (weights *and* the runtime that captured its logits),
KL direction, estimator precision, scope policy (what was quantized vs left native), and
measurement lane. The registry encodes this in two layers: the seven-field
`comparability.key` is a NECESSARY partition key -- rows with different keys render in
separate tables and must never be ranked against each other -- and a per-group
machine-readable predicate in the registry's `index.json` (`comparable: true/false/unknown`
plus reasons) covers what the key deliberately omits: lane, candidate pipeline, hardware,
artifact scope. Equal keys alone are NOT a license to rank; check the predicate. If you
cannot state the tuple for a number you found in the wild, it is an anecdote, not a
measurement.

**Rule 2 — never quote a single window as a rate comparison.** Per-window KLD scatter on our
panel (sd ≈ 1.7e-3) exceeds the difference between adjacent bit-widths (K6 vs K8 ≈ 1.2e-3).
One unlucky window made our 8-bit quant look *worse* than our 6-bit; the full 25-window panel
showed it winning decisively. Previews are for "is the pipeline alive", never for ranking.

**Rule 3 — subtract only a same-lane floor.** Scoring the *unquantized* weights against the
teacher already costs 0.011506 nats on our streaming lane (0.012712 cross-stack): that is the
price of the comparison itself, not quantization error. Attributable error = row − same-lane
floor. Subtracting a floor measured on a different lane is invalid and the validator refuses
it (invariant BIAS-006).

**Rule 4 — raw KLD understates differences between good quants.** Because the floor is common
to both, two strong quants look closer than they are. Ours differ 1.11× raw and 2.52× in
attributable error. Report both, or report attributable and name the floor.

**Rule 5 — measure the artifact or the serving stack, and say which.** The *checkpoint lane*
runs a reference `transformers` forward and characterizes the weights (it is bitwise
deterministic; five cold runs give population stddev exactly 0.0). The *serving lane* runs the
real engine and characterizes weights + kernels + activation quantization together. Neither is
wrong; mixing them silently is.

## Start here

- [WHAT-WE-MEASURE.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/WHAT-WE-MEASURE.md): the definitive answer to *what* a number here is — the measured quantity, whether the lm_head is included (yes in the computation, no in the quantization), the two lanes, floors, and the comparability rules. Read this before citing any number.
- [README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/README.md): repository overview and the copy-paste measurement recipes.
- [registry README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/registry/README.md): the measurement tables, grouped by comparability key, generated from the data (never hand-written).

## Measure a quant

- [bin/README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/bin/README.md): every CLI, its flags, and what each refusal means.
- `bin/measure --model <hf-repo>`: one command. Resolves the revision and lineage, checks whether the artifact is **already measured** (prints the existing rows and exits rather than spending), picks the panel, and runs. Start with `--dry-run`.
- `bin/measure-cloud`: rents a GPU, measures, tears down, and reports cost four ways. Teardown is guaranteed on success, failure, exception and Ctrl-C, with an on-instance watchdog as backstop.
- `bin/measure-local`: your own hardware. Works on Apple Silicon via MPS (decode is bitwise identical to CPU) and on a 32 GB consumer CUDA card under a `--vram-budget` that is a hard bound.
- `bin/registry-view`: query the published registry — filter by model, artifact, panel, lane, or who measured it — against a local clone or the live dataset.
- [FIDELITY-DATASET-SPEC.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/docs/FIDELITY-DATASET-SPEC.md): the three-step model — capture a reference dataset, capture a candidate dataset, compare them. Captures are publishable artifacts, so a comparison needs no GPU and no access to our infrastructure.

## Machine-readable data (prefer these over parsing prose)

- [measurements.jsonl](https://huggingface.co/datasets/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-registry/raw/main/data/measurements.jsonl): every measurement with its comparability key, lane, run count, determinism evidence, disclosed deviations and receipt link.
- [artifacts.jsonl](https://huggingface.co/datasets/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-registry/raw/main/data/artifacts.jsonl), [panels.jsonl](https://huggingface.co/datasets/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-registry/raw/main/data/panels.jsonl), [references.jsonl](https://huggingface.co/datasets/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-registry/raw/main/data/references.jsonl), [pipelines.jsonl](https://huggingface.co/datasets/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-registry/raw/main/data/pipelines.jsonl): the records a measurement points at. A measurement cannot exist without a panel and a reference.
- [JSON Schemas + invariants](https://github.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/tree/main/registry/schema): the rules the validator enforces, including the ones that refuse cross-lane floor subtraction and unbacked determinism claims.
- [CARD-ANNOTATION-SPEC.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/docs/CARD-ANNOTATION-SPEC.md): how a model card declares its fidelity provenance, as a conformant HF `model-index` result plus an `x_fidelity` block. Read a card's `model-index` to get its KLD without bespoke code.

## Contribute a measurement

- [docs/THIRD-PARTY-QUICKSTART.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/docs/THIRD-PARTY-QUICKSTART.md): the unaided first-time path — prerequisites with install commands, `bin/fidelity-doctor` as the one verification command, a named measurable target with a pinned revision, the fail-closed dry-run, the exact spend-confirmation prompt, and the one live submission destination.
- [registry/CONTRIBUTING.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/registry/CONTRIBUTING.md): what a receipt must contain, the submission template, and how you are credited. A measurement costs roughly $6–15 of rented GPU time. The sealed `measurement-receipt.json` a runner writes IS the submission receipt — one noun, one file.
- `bin/registry-submit <receipt.json>`: prints the row your receipt generates, its comparability key, and which existing rows it may be ranked against — or exactly which check it failed.

## Optional

- [JOURNAL.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/JOURNAL.md): the campaign log — every decision, failure, cost, and 30+ numbered lessons. Useful if you are debugging a similar pipeline; most lessons are about ways a measurement can be silently wrong.
- [engines/BF16-FLOOR.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/engines/BF16-FLOOR.md): how the floor was measured and the ways subtracting it can be misused.
- [engines/K8-ANOMALY.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/engines/K8-ANOMALY.md): the investigation behind Rule 2 — why an 8-bit quant appeared worse than a 6-bit one on one window.
- [docs/PROTOCOL-ALIGNMENT.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/docs/PROTOCOL-ALIGNMENT.md): element-by-element alignment with brandonmusic's proposed community standard, including where his protocol is stricter than ours and what we adopted.
- [docs/GGUF-MEASUREMENT.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/docs/GGUF-MEASUREMENT.md): why a llama.cpp GGUF row answers a different question from every other row in the streaming lane. A GGUF quantizes the whole forward -- embeddings, attention, dense MLPs and lm_head as well as the routed experts -- so it is not rankable against a routed-experts-only quant at "the same" bpw, and its nominal rate is not its measured one (a "Q4_K_XL" build measures 4.98 bits/weight). Also: why a build NAME does not tell you what types are inside it.
- [docs/ARCHITECTURE-DETERMINISM.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE-DETERMINISM.md): the same artifact, the same sealed panel, the same software stack -- and a different number on a different GPU. Two A100s in two clouds agree bitwise; an H200 is 2.973e-04 nats away, which is 13x the gap this registry publishes between two 4-bit quantizers. Eight cards were probed layer by layer: the divergence starts in the GEMM, no divergent quantity is a function of compute capability alone, and `use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` changes nothing across devices. Read it before comparing two numbers measured on different hardware.
- [engines/HANDOFF.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/engines/HANDOFF.md): twenty operational lessons for running a quantization or measurement campaign.
- [docs/CAPTURE-SCALING-PLAN.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/docs/CAPTURE-SCALING-PLAN.md): how a capture is scaled and what it costs — including why splitting a layer across GPUs produces a different measurement rather than a faster one.
